title: Russian — MVD Order No. 310 (Russian passports 1997–2010)
authority: MVD Russia Order No. 310 of 26.05.1997 (Instruction on passports for travel abroad); MVD Order No. 1047 of 31.12.2003
description: Diacritic-free, English-oriented system of the MVD passport instruction (Order No. 310 of 26 May 1997, re-issued by Order No. 1047 of 2003), used in Russian international passports until 2010: Й→Y, Ю→YU, Я→YA, ЬЕ/ЬЁ→YE, Ъ→", Ь→'.
notes: The primary text of Order No. 310 could not be retrieved; the table follows iuliia (which cites docs.cntd.ru) and Wikipedia.
Documented rules: ЬЕ and ЬЁ → YE (Васильева → Vasilyeva); ЪЕ → YE is taken from iuliia. iuliia's JSON implements only ЬЕ/ЪЕ, so for ЬЁ it gives Solov'ev where this scheme gives Solovyev.
Endings: ИЙ is either IY or Y and ЫЙ either YY or Y; this scheme uses the letter-by-letter IY/YY (Dmitriy, Vidnyy). Alternatives: Dmitry, Vidny.
ЕЙ may be EY or YEY; this scheme uses EY (Sergey, as in the Order No. 1047 example Сергей/Sergey).
Е is E at word start (Evgeniy, Ekaterina); iuliia lists 'ye,e' for Е/Ё but documents YE only after Ь.
Ъ/Ь: iuliia gives " and '; Wikipedia's comparison table gives ʺ for Ъ and omits Ь. Apostrophes were typically not printed in practice (and are never allowed in the MRZ).
samples: Юлия, съешь ещё этих мягких французских булок из Йошкар-Олы, да выпей алтайского чаю
Yuliya, syesh' eshche etikh myagkikh frantsuzskikh bulok iz Yoshkar-Oly, da vypey altayskogo chayu
